summary: Strengthened the new compaction finding with its normative basis, rather than merely an absence. The repository's own documentation states the duty and shows how it is discharged: docs/omnipaxos/compaction.md opens with 'As time passes, the replicated log in OmniPaxos will grow large. To avoid letting the log growing infinitely large, we support two ways of compaction that can be initiated by users' and its example calls omni_paxos.trim(...) on the instance (compaction.md:1-11), backed by OmniPaxos::trim/snapshot (omni_paxos.rs:242-262). Against that duty, the actor layer removes the path: spawn_actor consumes the instance by value (handle.rs:295), the handle keeps only channels and a capacity with no accessor back and no compaction method, the client protocol has no compaction request (Command = Append, AppendNotify, CurrentLeader, DecidedIdx, ReadDecidedSuffix, SubscribeDecided, Reconfigure, TryBecomeLeader, Reconnected — event.rs:90-128), and the actor never calls op.trim()/op.snapshot() (its only trim is trim_oldest over its own outgoing buffer). The account for that question now reads as an omitted duty of the layer that owns the instance — a runtime-only user's log can only grow — with the limits kept: source-only (no execution), the consequence not measured and the storage backend's fill-up behaviour unexamined, and no source stating compaction is deliberately out of scope, while the layer does expose other core-facing operations so this is a specific omission rather than a policy. Standing position unchanged: the event-backpressure park and cluster stall (capacities 8/64/1024, corrected transport, 21.69s retrospective bound), the core's missing accept-phase repair for a lost Accepted (2-node scope), and append_notify's false Ok for an unadopted index with the adopted-vs-unadopted boundary measured.
